candidates.attacker_control: A remote STOMP-over-WebSocket client fully controls the value of the custom 'selector' header on a SUBSCRIBE frame (StompDecoder.readHeaders copies arbitrary client header names/values into the native-header map, restricted only by header syntax). NativeMessageHeaderAccessor.addNativeHeader performs no name blacklisting, so 'selector' is accepted. The same client (or any other client) can trigger evaluation by sending a SEND frame to the destination it subscribed to.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that parse errors are caught and skip evaluation (expression stays null) - only valid expressions are needed; checked that evaluation requires selectorHeaderInUse - the attacker's own subscription sets it and the attacker can send the triggering SEND itself; checked that the registry is only used by the simple broker (SimpleBrokerMessageHandler line 83) and that the broker subscribes to clientInboundChannel (AbstractBrokerMessageHandler.start line 159); checked that STOMP header-name restrictions do not block 'selector' (NativeMessageHeaderAccessor.addNativeHeader lines 171-188; no override in StompHeaderAccessor); checked that a restricted evaluation context exists but is unused (SimpleEvaluationContext @since 4.3.15 appears nowhere else in the tree), i.e. the hardening is not yet applied to this path.
candidates.impact: Remote code execution in the JVM/OS user running the application server (arbitrary commands/reflection), i.e. full host compromise, triggered by an unauthenticated (or low-privileged authenticated) network client of the WebSocket endpoint. Even if the boolean conversion later throws, the attacker-chosen expression has already been evaluated.
candidates.prerequisites: Application exposes STOMP over WebSocket with the in-memory simple broker (standard @EnableWebSocketMessageBroker + enableSimpleBroker("/topic", ...) setup; SimpleBrokerMessageHandler creates DefaultSubscriptionRegistry by default and subscribes to the client inbound channel). No authentication or special role is required; the subscription must be registered on a destination matching the broker's configured prefix and the triggering SEND must reach that same destination. A well-formed SpEL expression is required (parse failures are caught). Applications that explicitly change selectorHeaderName would need the attacker to use that name; applications using the broker relay (StompBrokerRelayMessageHandler) instead of the simple broker do not use this path.
candidates.root_cause: DefaultSubscriptionRegistry (spring-messaging) treats the client-supplied 'selector' STOMP header as a Spring EL expression. The header name is enabled by default (field selectorHeaderName = "selector", line 72), and the expression is evaluated at message-dispatch time with an unrestricted StandardEvaluationContext (lines 211-216), which permits SpEL type references (T(...)), constructors and arbitrary reflective method invocation. The only guard is parsing/evaluation error logging (lines 153-157, 220-227); evaluation side effects occur before any boolean conversion failure is swallowed. A restricted context (SimpleEvaluationContext, which excludes type references/constructors/bean references) exists in spring-expression at the snapshot but is unused in spring-messaging.
candidates.title: Remote code execution via client-controlled SpEL 'selector' header in STOMP subscription registry
candidates.trace: STOMP SUBSCRIBE frame -> StompDecoder.readHeaders (lines 228-238) stores 'selector' in the native headers -> StompSubProtocolHandler.handleMessageFromClient (lines 271-299) forwards the message with native headers to clientInboundChannel -> SimpleBrokerMessageHandler.handleMessageInternal SUBSCRIBE branch (lines 285-288) calls subscriptionRegistry.registerSubscription -> AbstractSubscriptionRegistry.registerSubscription -> DefaultSubscriptionRegistry.addSubscriptionInternal (lines 139-161) reads getFirstNativeHeader("selector") and parses it as SpEL at line 147, setting selectorHeaderInUse = true -> subsequent SEND frame: SimpleBrokerMessageHandler.sendMessageToSubscribers (line 333) -> SubscriptionRegistry.findSubscriptions -> DefaultSubscriptionRegistry.filterSubscriptions (lines 188-231), which builds new StandardEvaluationContext(message) (line 212) and calls expression.getValue(context, boolean.class) (line 216) -> arbitrary SpEL (e.g. type references and reflective invocation) is executed during evaluation; resulting errors are swallowed at lines 220-227 after the side effect has already occurred.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed, built, or tested, and no runtime exploit was attempted; reachability is established by source-level call-chain tracing only. The mapping of this snapshot to the specific upstream fix commit/CVE (4.3.15 selector fix, CVE-2018-1270/1275) is inferred from the version string (4.3.15.BUILD-SNAPSHOT) and the presence of the unused SimpleEvaluationContext (@since 4.3.15), not from commit metadata. Applicability depends on the deployed Spring configuration (simple broker over STOMP/WebSocket); an app using the broker relay or an explicitly renamed/disabled selector header is not affected by this exact header.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression Language Injection / Code Injection (CWE-917, CWE-94)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 7,287 files under the assigned root; 7,286 model-visible files; 1 excluded by sensitive-name/path filter; 0 files over 5 MiB; 0 symlinks; binary-like files are skipped/refused. The P1 relation index is partial: 6,412 Java files indexed, 395 omitted, syntax-only relations (containment, name/type/arity-based call and inheritance candidates), control flow and data flow explicitly not implemented, 184,210 unresolved calls, Spring DI/security enforcement unverified. I reviewed the spring-messaging broker/STOMP/SpEL paths in detail (DefaultSubscriptionRegistry, AbstractSubscriptionRegistry, SimpleBrokerMessageHandler, AbstractBrokerMessageHandler, StompDecoder, StompHeaderAccessor, NativeMessageHeaderAccessor, SimpleEvaluationContext), the spring-websocket StompSubProtocolHandler inbound path, and sampled spring-webmvc resource handling and spring-web multipart classes; I did not review the majority of the remaining ~7,000 files (e.g. full spring-orm/jms/oxm/test modules, most spring-web/http converters) line by line.
limitations: No code was executed, built, or tested; all conclusions are source-text based and no runtime confirmation exists.

The P1 relation index is syntactic only (no data/control flow, partial file coverage, unresolved calls); every edge used was re-verified against source text, but index omissions mean unreported areas were not automatically cleared.

No web access or external services were used, so upstream fix commits, CVE identifiers and release-note content are not independently verified; the snapshot-to-CVE mapping is inferred from version 4.3.15.BUILD-SNAPSHOT and the unused @since 4.3.15 SimpleEvaluationContext.

Exploitability of the selector path depends on runtime deployment configuration (STOMP WebSocket endpoint + simple broker), which cannot be confirmed from this tree alone; servlet-container-specific behavior relevant to the rejected multipart lead is likewise unverifiable here.
Coverage is strongest for spring-messaging/spring-websocket/spring-expression and sampled web resource/multipart code; large parts of the repository were not inspected in depth.

rejected_leads.lead: Static-resource directory traversal in spring-webmvc (CVE-2018-1271 class, Windows backslash/encoded traversal)
rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot already contains encoded-path defenses: ResourceHttpRequestHandler.getResource rejects invalid decoded paths (isInvalidPath at 643-663, isInvalidEncodedPath at 604-625) and PathResourceResolver.isResourceUnderLocation calls isInvalidEncodedPath (lines 248, 283-306); traversal/encoded-path tests exist in ResourceHttpRequestHandlerTests and PathResourceResolverTests. I could not construct a source-level bypass, and the Windows-specific semantics cannot be verified read-only; left unconfirmed rather than submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: Multipart request parameter handling inconsistency in spring-web (CVE-2018-1272 class)
rejected_leads.reason: In StandardMultipartHttpServletRequest.getParameterMap (lines 197-216) multipart parameter names are merged only when absent from the container map, while getParameter/getParameterValues behavior is delegated to the container and DefaultMultipartHttpServletRequest.getParameter (lines 78-94) prefers multipart values - a genuine inconsistency. However, exploitability depends on servlet-container multipart parsing semantics that are not visible in this source tree and no concrete security-check bypass could be established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Odd 'separatorIndex' logic in PathResourceResolver.isInvalidEncodedPath (lines 288-297) that returns true for almost any decoded '..' occurrence
rejected_leads.reason: Analysis shows the odd code is fail-closed (over-rejecting, e.g. it rejects benign names containing '..' before a non-separator character) rather than a bypass; not a security weakness in the attacker's favor.

summary: Reviewed the assigned Spring Framework snapshot (version 4.3.15.BUILD-SNAPSHOT; 7,286 visible files, 6,412 Java). Focus was spring-messaging (broker/STOMP), spring-websocket (STOMP sub-protocol), spring-expression (SpEL), plus sampling of spring-web/spring-webmvc resource and multipart handling. The single strongest candidate is a client-controlled SpEL injection in DefaultSubscriptionRegistry: a remote STOMP client can place a SpEL expression in the "selector" native header of a SUBSCRIBE frame (enabled by default), and that expression is later evaluated with an unrestricted StandardEvaluationContext on message dispatch, enabling remote code execution via SpEL type references/reflection. This matches the CVE-2018-1270/1275 class fixed in 4.3.15/5.0.5; notably this same snapshot already contains the newly added (a 4.3.15) but completely unused SimpleEvaluationContext class, whose purpose is to exclude type references, constructors and bean references - consistent with a snapshot taken just before the fix that restricts or disables this selector evaluation.
